title: Hidden Data Challenges in Clinical Machine Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.13350v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Widely reused preprocessing pipelines for electronic health records can encode assumptions about when information became available, what clinical episode a label represents, and what missingness means. These assumptions are rarely audited systematically and may propagate across subsequent studies when preprocessing pipelines are reused or adapted. Using MIMIC-IV as a case study, we identify and quantify violations of three complementary forms of preprocessing alignment, i.e., temporal, semantic, and population alignment, which manifest as temporal leakage, feature-task misalignment, and biased imputation. We show how ambiguities in timestamp semantics, episode definitions, endpoint construction, modality selection, and missingness handling can alter the information available to a model and affect the interpretation of its predictions. translated_title: 临床机器学习中的隐性数据挑战
translated_abstract: 被广泛复用的电子健康记录预处理流水线可能隐含着关于信息何时可用、标签代表何种临床事件片段、以及缺失值含义的假设。这些假设很少得到系统性审计，并且当预处理流水线被复用或改编时，可能会在后续研究中传播。我们以MIMIC-IV为案例研究，识别并量化了三种互补的预处理对齐形式（即时间对齐、语义对齐和人群对齐）的违规情况，它们分别表现为时间泄漏、特征-任务错位和有偏插补。我们展示了时间戳语义、事件片段定义、终点构建、模态选择和缺失值处理中的模糊性如何改变模型可获取的信息，并影响对其预测结果的解释。通过对MIMIC-IV数据的分析和实证案例研究，我们证明了这些数据处理选择可能仍然……
tldr: 该论文以MIMIC-IV为案例，系统揭示并量化了临床机器学习中广泛复用的预处理流水线在时间、语义和人群对齐上的隐性假设违规——包括时间泄漏、特征-任务错位和有偏插补——并说明这些模糊的数据处理选择会如何改变模型可见的信息并影响预测解释。
en_tdlr: Using MIMIC-IV as a case study, this paper systematically identifies and quantifies hidden violations of temporal, semantic, and population alignment in widely reused clinical ML preprocessing pipelines—manifesting as temporal leakage, feature-task misalignment, and biased imputation—and shows how ambiguous data processing choices can alter the information available to models and their prediction interpretation.
